title: Optimizing Distributed ML Communication with Fused Computation-Collective Operations
problem: Collective communication is often the critical bottleneck in distributed ML training across multiple nodes. Without independent computation kernels executing concurrently, communication latency cannot be hidden through overlap.
motivation: Reducing communication overhead is essential to improving scalability and efficiency of distributed machine learning training.
method: The approach fuses computation with subsequent collective communication operations, allowing threadblocks to immediately communicate results to remote GPUs via GPU-initiated communication while other workgroups continue computation. Three prototype fused operators are developed: embedding+All-to-All, GEMV+AllReduce, and GEMM+All-to-All, targeting DLRM, Transformer, and MoE architectures. These are exposed as PyTorch operators and integrated into the Triton framework.
key_novelty: Fusing computation directly with collective operations at the threadblock granularity, enabling simultaneous communication and computation within a single GPU kernel via GPU-initiated communication.
contributions: Fused computation-collective operator design that overlaps communication with computation
Three prototype implementations targeting major ML architectures (DLRM, Transformers, MoE)
Integration as PyTorch operators and Triton framework extensions
12-31% execution time reduction across all three fused operators
primary_theme: overlapping communication and computation in distributed ML via fused kernels
